mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate increases borrowing costs, which may reduce consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE increases by 0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates reduced demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when HOUST decreases by 5% YoY, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO increases by 1% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate stimulates economic activity by reducing borrowing costs, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.25%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS increases by 100,000 jobs, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real federal funds rate and a decrease in consumer price index suggests reduced inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% and CPIAUCSL decreases by 0.1%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% and CPIAUCSL decreases by 0.1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production and an increase in unemployment rate signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by 0.5% MoM and UNRATE increases by 0.2pp
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO decreases by 0.5% MoM and UNRATE increases by 0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.
